name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Deborah Ross with large cash advantage
Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: Ross holds a D+17 district, a $1.3 million war chest against a challenger with no reported fundraising, and no outside spending against her; markets price her at 99%. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a dramatically different environment or unexpected outside spending against Ross would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross seeks reelection in a Raleigh-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She enters the general election with roughly $1.3 million on hand, while Republican Eugene Douglass has no reported fundraising and no outside groups are active in the race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and prediction markets that price Ross at about 99%. The expected margin is roughly 24 points, making this one of the safest Democratic House seats up this cycle.
